title: Primary Function
learningObjectives: Identify the structural purpose of the bonded joint.
student: State the primary structural function of the bonded plate joint.
instructor: The joint transfers axial load from one primary plate into two overlapping splice plates while maintaining continuity and alignment of the larger structural assembly.

title: External Loads
learningObjectives: Identify the applied end loads and their directions.
student: Identify the external axial loads and explain what condition they must satisfy for equilibrium.
instructor: PA acts to the left at A. PB1 and PB2 act to the right at B. Equilibrium requires PA = PB1 + PB2.

title: Boundary Conditions
learningObjectives: Describe the boundary conditions used in the simplified model.
student: Describe the boundary conditions used in the simplified one-dimensional model.
instructor: The assembly is loaded by equal and opposite axial resultants at its ends. No transverse supports, shear forces, or bending moments are included in the one-dimensional deformation model.

title: Load Path
learningObjectives: Trace axial force through the built-up joint.
student: Trace the load path from end A through the overlap and to end B.
instructor: The load enters the primary plate at A, travels through its single-plate region, transfers through the bonded overlap into the upper and lower splice plates, and exits through the two loads at B.

title: Mechanically Distinct Regions
learningObjectives: Divide the joint into constant-area regions.
student: Identify the mechanically distinct regions needed for a piecewise axial-deformation model.
instructor: Region 1 contains one active plate, Region 2 contains three bonded plates in the overlap, and Region 3 contains the two outgoing splice plates.

title: Relevant Mechanical Response
learningObjectives: Distinguish the base deformation response from excluded local behavior.
student: What response is evaluated in the base problem, and what local joint behavior is excluded?
instructor: The base problem evaluates total axial deformation. Bond-line shear and peel stress, seam-end stress concentrations, local plate bending, and bond slip are intentionally excluded.

title: Relevant Parameters
learningObjectives: Identify the inputs controlling piecewise axial deformation.
student: List the loading, geometric, and material parameters that control the joint deformation.
instructor: The governing inputs are the three end loads, segment lengths L1 through L3, plate width w, plate thickness t, the number of active plates in each region, and elastic modulus E.

title: Student-Generated Structural Idealization
learningObjectives: Create a one-dimensional model before viewing the reference figure.
student: Before using the reference figure, create a one-dimensional axial model with three constant-area regions. Label the end loads, region boundaries, lengths, and effective areas.
instructor: A valid model shows Region 1 with area wt, Region 2 with area 3wt, Region 3 with area 2wt, the three segment lengths, and the applied end loads.
gradingNotes: Students should attempt the load-path and region model before seeing the instructor idealization.

title: Modeling Assumptions
learningObjectives: State assumptions supporting the effective-area model.
student: State the assumptions required for the simplified axial-deformation analysis.
instructor: Assume linear-elastic plates of uniform width and thickness, uniform average axial stress in each effective section, perfect bond and equal axial strain among overlapping plates, small deformation, and negligible local stress concentration, bond slip, and bending.

title: Mechanics Analysis Plan
student: Outline the calculation sequence before carrying out numerical work.
instructor: Verify load equilibrium, determine the internal axial force, identify each effective area, compute each segment deformation from δi = NiLi/(AiE), and sum the signed segment deformations.

title: Load Equilibrium and Sharing
learningObjectives: Verify equilibrium and compatibility of the assigned loads.
student: Using the assigned values, verify overall axial equilibrium and assess the load sharing between the identical outgoing plates.
instructor: The outgoing resultant is {{plate_load_sum_B_kN}} kN, and the signed residual PB1 + PB2 - PA is {{plate_load_residual_kN}} kN. {{plate_equilibrium_assessment}} {{plate_load_sharing_assessment}}

title: Internal Axial-Force Diagram
learningObjectives: Determine the axial resultant in each region.
student: Determine the internal axial-force magnitude in each region and describe the force carried by each outgoing plate.
instructor: The region resultants are N1 = {{plate_N1_kN}} kN, N2 = {{plate_N2_kN}} kN, and N3 = {{plate_N3_kN}} kN. In Region 3, the upper and lower plates carry the assigned loads PB1 and PB2.

title: Effective Cross-Sectional Areas
learningObjectives: Calculate effective area from the number of active plates.
student: Determine the effective load-carrying area of each region.

title: Segment-Deformation Equations
learningObjectives: Write a consistent deformation equation for each region.
student: Write the axial-deformation equation for each segment and state the required unit conversion for the elastic modulus.
instructor: Use δi = NiLi/(AiE) for each constant-area region. With force in newtons and geometry in millimeters, convert E from GPa to MPa, where 1 GPa = 1000 N/mm2.

title: Segment Deformations
student: Calculate the axial deformation of each region.
instructor: The tensile elongations are δ1 = {{plate_delta_1_mm}} mm, δ2 = {{plate_delta_2_mm}} mm, and δ3 = {{plate_delta_3_mm}} mm.
commonMistakes: Do not use the single-plate area in all three regions, and convert kN to N and GPa to MPa.

title: Relative Displacement of A and B
learningObjectives: Sum segment deformations and interpret the displacement sign.
student: Determine the total change in separation between A and B. Then report uA - uB using rightward displacement as positive.
instructor: The A-B separation increases by {{plate_delta_total_mm}} mm. With rightward displacement positive, uA - uB = {{plate_relative_A_B_mm}} mm.
gradingNotes: Accept a positive 0.491 mm if the student clearly defines that value as the increase in separation rather than uA - uB.

title: Governing Deformation Contribution
learningObjectives: Relate deformation contribution to length and effective area.
student: Identify which region contributes most to the total displacement and explain why.
instructor: {{plate_governing_region}} governs with {{plate_governing_delta_mm}} mm, or approximately {{plate_governing_percent}}% of the total deformation. The dominant contribution follows from the segment ratio L/(AE).

title: Stiffness-Based Modification
learningObjectives: Recommend a modification based on the governing compliance.
student: Recommend one modification that would reduce joint displacement without changing the applied load.
instructor: Increase width or thickness in the most compliant region, particularly Region 1 for the baseline geometry. This increases AE/L directly. Merely lengthening the overlap is not automatically the best change unless it replaces a more compliant region with the higher-area overlap.

title: Engineering Assessment and Model Scope
learningObjectives: Make a bounded recommendation and identify omitted checks.
student: Provide a concise engineering assessment and identify the additional checks required before approving a real bonded splice.
instructor:
{{plate_recommendation}}

A complete design must also check bond-line shear and peel stress, seam-end stress concentration, plate yielding, bond strength and slip, fatigue, environmental durability, local bending, and manufacturing quality.
gradingNotes: The assessment must not claim that the joint is safe without a displacement limit and the omitted strength checks.
